obligations.source_text: Causal links resolve through origin markers stamped by actions, generalizing the marker contract in examples/jira-question-round-trip/question_correlation.py. obligations.source_text: Chaining carries causal context: when trigger B fires on something action A produced, B's run can read the variables of the declaration run that led to A (e.g. 'PR spec created' knows the Jira issue behind the intake that committed the PR).

obligations.behavior: Re-entry beyond the trigger's limit (default 3, 0 = none), hop-limit breach, unopted self-retrigger, or rate breach stops the chain and writes a visible record.
obligations.source_text: Loop protection works on causal lineage (c40, c43). The re-entry limit (c51) is declared on the trigger, defaulting to 3 appearances of the same declaration in one lineage, with 0 meaning the declaration may not re-appear in its own lineage. Backstops: a hop limit on total lineage depth, no self-retrigger unless the declaration opts in, and a per-declaration rate ceiling. Hitting any limit stops the chain and raises a visible record for a human, never a silent drop. Generalizes jira_comment_is_self_echo, maxTransitions/maxVisitsPerNode, the repair bound (internal/repair) and subject deferral (deferred_triggers).

obligations.behavior: Refuses an activation declaration activating itself or another by the same author; the first activation declaration requires a human principal.
obligations.source_text: Activation policy is itself a set of declarations (q13), and those activation declarations are the root of trust: an activation declaration cannot activate itself or another activation declaration it authored, and the first ones are activated by a human. Without this, an agent could declare 'activate everything I propose', self-activate it, and hold standing authority to post, comment, dispatch or run code with no human ever having granted it (PRD §10.4: no actor promotes its own proposal).

obligations.behavior: Each firing records the declaration id and the version digests of the trigger, condition and action it evaluated; old versions stay fetchable.
obligations.source_text: Every declaration version is immutable and content-addressed (internal/contracts/canonical.go). The pin moves from the run to the firing: each firing records the exact version it evaluated (trigger, condition, action), so a live upgrade never rewrites history and 'which version did this?' is always answerable. A new version applies from the next firing, including in chains already in flight (q16). This deviates from PRD §9.1/§9.10 'runs pin an immutable digest' and is recorded in the ADR (c21).

obligations.behavior: Implements the grammar: first segment is the step (0 = this run, N back, or a declaration name), value else default else verbatim placeholder, {N:x:} empty, {{ escapes a brace.
obligations.source_text: Template grammar: the first segment is always the step, 0 = this run: {owner}, {0:owner:x}, {1:owner}, {jira-intake:owner:}. A literal brace is escaped as {{.

obligations.behavior: Every declaration operation has one API route and one CLI verb with --json; the CLI holds no declaration logic.
obligations.source_text: The CLI and API let a user or an agent declare new declarations and build graphs from them, so agents and humans have clear control over what exists.

obligations.behavior: Verifies the GitHub signature, refuses unsigned payloads, and emits github.pr.approved exactly once per approval (redelivery deduplicated); the poller emits the same event name and payload shape.
obligations.source_text: 'GitHub PR approved' becomes a trigger. Today it is not detectable: there is no GitHub webhook receiver, and the pr-upkeep sweep (examples/pr-upkeep/sweep.py, pr_upkeep_emit.py) emits only pr.opened / pr.merged / pr.closed; readiness.py reads unresolved threads, never reviewDecision.

obligations.behavior: A created issue yields exactly one jira.issue.created across both sources.
obligations.source_text: 'Jira issue created' becomes a named trigger. Today creation surfaces only indirectly, as a synthetic pr-upkeep.jira.transitioned.<initial-status> with from_status '' built from fields.created (internal/api/jirawebhook.go jiraEmissions), and trigger event names carry the pr-upkeep.* prefix of the loop that first needed them.

obligations.behavior: A before/after switch selects the graph engine or the declaration engine per namespace, is reversible, and is recorded when flipped.
obligations.source_text: All existing workflows are migrated, with a before/after toggle between the old graph engine and the new declaration engine.

obligations.behavior: Runs code in a separate process with a timeout; a hanging or crashing script never stalls the control plane.
obligations.source_text: 'On the server' means a built-in runner on the control-plane host, in a separate sandboxed process (headspace-style workspace), never inside the control-plane process. This keeps c19: a hung, crashing or hostile script cannot stall or tamper with the service that holds authoritative state. Remote runners are registered and offered like agent actors.

obligations.behavior: Reports every pair of active declarations on the same node with the same trigger and possibly-overlapping conditions, in show/focus, and emits declaration.overlap when configured.
obligations.source_text: When two declarations share similar conditions (overlapping trigger and condition), the user can see it, or be notified of it.

obligations.behavior: A redelivered event id fires nothing twice; a re-minted firing keeps its lineage and counts once toward re-entry.
obligations.source_text: Lineage survives at-least-once delivery: a redelivered event with the same event id is deduplicated (signal_event_watermarks) and never fires a declaration twice; a re-minted trigger (trigger_remints) keeps the original lineage, so must-appear-after and re-entry counts see one chain, not two.

obligations.behavior: A waiting node whose reacting declaration no longer matches closes with an 'orphaned by upgrade' record naming both versions.
obligations.source_text: An in-flight node (an action called, its reaction not yet captured) keeps the version that called the action; the reaction is evaluated by whatever versions are current when it arrives. If the upgrade removed the declaration or changed its trigger so the reaction no longer matches, the node closes with a visible 'orphaned by upgrade vN' record, never a silent drop.

obligations.behavior: Refuses a move or nest that creates an alias cycle, naming the cycle.
obligations.source_text: Alias nesting is checked at write time: a move or nest that would make an alias contain itself, directly or through other aliases, is refused with the cycle named.

obligations.behavior: Returns exactly the declarations within N hops in both directions across must and can links, filterable by direction and link type; nodes are not hops.
obligations.source_text: Q11 proposal: distance counts hops in both directions (what leads here and what follows), across both must and can links, with filters for direction and link type. Distance is measured over declarations; nodes are drawn but do not count as hops.

obligations.behavior: Only a human principal activates an activation declaration; an activation declaration's action may target only ordinary declarations, refused at publish otherwise.
obligations.source_text: Activation declarations are the root of trust, and the chain is one level deep: only a human principal can activate an activation declaration, and an activation declaration may only activate ordinary declarations, never another activation declaration. Without this, an agent could propose 'activate everything' and have it activated by a broader human-activated rule, or two agents could activate each other's rules, holding standing authority to post, comment, dispatch or run code that no human granted (PRD §10.4). The owner accepts this as the current rule and may relax it later.
